clue.text: Existing from the beginning, or mid-April possibly

indicators.note: possibly says these letters are just one possible arrangement, so they are to be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, hyphen ignored

explanation.surface: A question about whether something dates from the dawn of time or merely from the middle of spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges the ten letters of OR MIDAPRIL; mid-April looks like a date but is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Primordial describes what was present at the very start of time or of a process.

clue.text: Money to pay for running bridge welcomed by bridge player

indicators.note: being welcomed by someone means being taken in by them, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: West is one of the four seats at a bridge table
an arch is a bridge-like span

explanation.surface: Funds for a race or a bridge construction project are received by a card player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' means running for office, a campaign; the card game supplies one of its compass-point players, North, South, East or West.
explanation.definitionFit: A war chest is a fund set aside to pay for a campaign, such as an election bid.

clue.text: Steps used in country's borders to contain force and reduce air traffic?

indicators.note: to contain means to hold something within, so the next piece goes inside

parts.note: a stile is a set of steps for crossing a fence or hedge on a field boundary in the countryside
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: A cryptic note about aviation: rural boundary steps must hold back power to cut flights.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful definition: 'air traffic' is breath, not aircraft, and to stifle someone is to stop their breathing.
explanation.definitionFit: To stifle is to smother or suffocate, which cuts off the flow of breath in and out.

clue.text: Did tramp spread it out?

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wondering question about whether a vagrant scattered something around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tramp' looks like a noun for a vagrant but is the verb, so 'Did tramp' is a past-tense definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Traipsed means walked wearily or trudged about, the same as tramped.

clue.text: Measure case to support British University without a single student

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits below, so the case comes after the other letters
without means lacking, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: a shell is an outer case
L for learner is a student driver; one of the two in the word is dropped

explanation.surface: A container is put under a British university that has lost one of its students.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for learner, as on British learner-driver plates; the case word has two of them, and 'a single student' says only one goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A bushel is an old unit of dry capacity, used for grain and fruit.

clue.text: Rich source belonging to the author

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the setter speaking of what is the writer's own

explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords 'the author' or 'the setter' is the person writing the clue, so what belongs to them is theirs in the first person.
explanation.definitionFit: A mine is a deposit yielding wealth, and the possessive pronoun says something is owned by the speaker.

clue.text: Inactive person's walked around outside

indicators.note: outside says one piece is placed round the other
around here means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: trod is a past tense of tread, to walk
person's is read as person is; a man is a person

explanation.surface: Someone sluggish has been out for a stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'person's' is 'person is', so the person is placed with DORT, TROD read backwards, around the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormant means temporarily asleep or not active, like a volcano that is not erupting.

clue.text: Material question introduced by lawyer close to victim

indicators.note: introduced by means preceded by, so the other pieces come first

parts.note: DA is the US district attorney

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

parts.note: its last letter is taken
to ask is to question

explanation.surface: A courtroom scene where a lawyer near the victim puts a question about fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: DA is the American district attorney, a public prosecutor.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a patterned woven fabric, often silk or linen, used for tablecloths and upholstery.

clue.text: Train, with money and uniform returned, to join forces again

indicators.note: with here says the train is given the new pieces in place of its own matching stretch

parts.note: a retinue is the train of attendants following an important person

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so these letters are read in the reverse direction

parts.note: tin is slang for money
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone trains up, with cash and kit given back, to rejoin an alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is that the train word already contains money and uniform side by side, so turning just that stretch round is all the change needed.
explanation.definitionFit: To reunite is to bring together once more people or groups who had been separated.

clue.text: Guarantee clubs being exempt from criticism

indicators.note: being exempt from means being free of, so the letter for clubs is removed

parts.note: censure is formal criticism
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: An assurance that golf or nightclubs will be spared condemnation.
explanation.walkthrough: The clubs are the card suit, which gives C, not golf clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure is to make certain that something happens, the verb sense of guarantee.

clue.text: Copy host content to limit charges

indicators.note: to charge is to load or fill, so the host is filled with the other piece

parts.note: MC is a master of ceremonies, a host

indicators.note: the content belonging to a word is its inside, everything but the first and last letters

parts.note: the inner letters of this word are used

explanation.surface: A host is happy to cap the fees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like 'happy' but means the contents, and 'charges' is a verb, loads, not fees.
explanation.definitionFit: To mimic is to imitate someone's manner or speech closely.

clue.text: Atheist has left and is upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nonbeliever has walked out and is distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like it should give L, but the whole word goes into the mix of HAS LEFT IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone faithless lacks religious faith, as an unbeliever does.

clue.text: She can spell "nineteenth shallow dish" out loud apparently

indicators.note: out loud says the words are spoken, and the result only sounds like the answer

parts.note: a saucer is a shallow dish, and the nineteenth letter of the alphabet, S, is spoken ess

explanation.surface: A schoolchild spelling test: can she spell a strange phrase?
explanation.walkthrough: 'spell' is magic, not writing. SAUCER said with ESS, the name of the alphabet's nineteenth letter, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorceress is a female magician, one who casts spells.

clue.text: Surgical equipment in casualty department of US city

parts.note: LA, Los Angeles, with the possessive 's for 'of'
ER is the emergency room, the US term for a hospital casualty department

explanation.surface: A piece of operating-theatre kit in a Los Angeles hospital's emergency ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of US city' reads as LA's, so the department belongs to Los Angeles.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasers are used in surgery to cut or seal tissue with a focused beam of light.

clue.text: Astonishing cast's left to be replaced by graffiti artist

indicators.note: one letter is swapped out and the other piece put in its place

parts.note: cast's is cast has; to sling is to cast or throw
a tagger sprays a signature tag as graffiti

explanation.surface: A theatre company's departure is amazingly followed by a street artist taking over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' is not a theatre troupe but the verb throw, and 'left' is not departed but L.
explanation.definitionFit: Staggering means so surprising that it almost knocks you off balance.

clue.text: Social media platform wanting wife to have a laugh

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the letter is removed

parts.note: Twitter is the social media site now called X

explanation.surface: A spouse is amused by something posted online.
explanation.definitionFit: To titter is to give a short, nervous or suppressed giggle.

clue.text: Communist-controlled state was left behind

indicators.note: being controlled means being held in check, so the state sits inside

parts.note: red is the colour and nickname of a communist
Maine is a US state

explanation.surface: A country run by communists stayed behind the times.
explanation.definitionFit: Remained means stayed put while others moved on.

clue.text: Gadget rotating plug in bonnet of Cadillac

indicators.note: rotating means turning round, so the combination is read backwards
in puts one piece inside another

parts.note: a car bonnet is called a hood in America, home of the Cadillac
an ad is a plug, a promotion

explanation.surface: A spinning plug stuck into the bonnet of an American car.
explanation.walkthrough: A bonnet is the British word for a car's engine cover; the American car points to the US word.
explanation.definitionFit: A doodah is an informal word for a thingummy, any object whose name escapes you.

clue.text: Honour soldier protecting lives and showing respect

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding as a guard, so the other piece goes inside

parts.note: OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire
a soldier ant
is means exists or lives

explanation.surface: A decorated soldier guards lives and is respectful.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is a British honour awarded by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeisant means deferential, bowing or giving homage.

clue.text: Masterly and concise description of gallery?

indicators.note: concise means cut short, so the final letter is trimmed

parts.note: a gallery is full of art, so it might be called art-full

explanation.surface: A gallery summed up briefly as skilful.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the whimsical description 'art-full'.
explanation.definitionFit: Artful means clever or skilful, often in a crafty way.

clue.text: Lively female broadcaster bored by religious programme

indicators.note: being bored by something means being drilled into, so the other piece goes inside

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite broadcaster
RI is religious instruction, a school subject

explanation.surface: A spirited woman presenter is bored by a church broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bored' looks like weary but means pierced; Sky is a British TV company.
explanation.definitionFit: Frisky means playful and full of energy.

clue.text: Roman Catholic priest wears holy artefact

indicators.note: to wear something is to have it around you, so RC goes around the priest

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel

explanation.surface: A Catholic cleric dons a sacred object.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is an object revered because it belonged to or touched a saint.

clue.text: Contribute feature in which Internet Protocol is encapsulated

indicators.note: in which points to the piece receiving the other
being encapsulated means enclosed, so this goes inside the feature

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: A tech article describing a feature that wraps network protocol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feature' sounds like software, but it is a facial feature.
explanation.definitionFit: To chip in is to add one's share, of money or comment.

clue.text: Person who delivers dog's dinner meets English Queen

parts.note: a dog's dinner is British slang for a mess
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A courier bringing a dog's meal encounters the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: A dog's dinner is British slang for a muddle; ER is Queen Elizabeth's cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: A messenger carries messages or packages to people.

clue.text: Contraceptive curbs passion in silence

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: sh is a call for silence
heat is passion

explanation.surface: Birth control quietly restrains desire.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath is a condom, a barrier contraceptive.

clue.text: Reproduction in dysfunctional families stopped by introduction of contraception

indicators.note: stopped by means plugged by, so the letter goes inside
dysfunctional means not working properly, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its first letter

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: Breeding in troubled households halted by the arrival of birth control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reproduction' looks like breeding but means a copy.
explanation.definitionFit: A facsimile is an exact copy of a document or object.

clue.text: Smart way to reduce energy

parts.note: a cut is a way to reduce
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A clever method for cutting power usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute can mean shrewd or clever, as in a cute move.

clue.text: Call for help about cuts and other wounds

indicators.note: cuts means slices into, so this piece goes inside

parts.note: SOS is a distress signal
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A distress call about lacerations and other injuries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts' looks like part of the injury list, but it is the verb putting RE into SOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sores are painful patches on the skin, a kind of wound other than cuts.

clue.text: Camp gents queue to hold a teenager's coat

indicators.note: to hold is to keep within, so the queue goes around

parts.note: a line is a queue

indicators.note: a coat is the outer layer, so the first and last letters

parts.note: the word teenager, the possessive pointing to its coat

explanation.surface: Men at camp line up to keep a youngster's coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gents' is British for a men's lavatory, so camp gents is a camp toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A latrine is a toilet in a camp or barracks, often a trench.

clue.text: Period of occupation gutted Toulouse and another French town

indicators.note: gutted means emptied of insides, leaving the first and last letters

parts.note: its first and last letters
Nancy is a city in north-eastern France

explanation.surface: An era when Toulouse and a second French town were ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenancy is the time during which a tenant occupies a property.
